# Current Research

## Bayes-Optimal Learning and Generative Modeling

Bayes Optimal Learning Threshold (BOLT) introduces a novel approach to design loss function: it derives a parameterized upper bound on the Bayes error rate and using its minimization to guide model training toward Bayes-optimal performance. Originally developed for classification, the BOLT framework has been extended to generative adversarial networks (BOLT-GAN). BOLT shows improved training stability and generative performance. Its underlying principle provides a general foundation for designing learning objectives across different learning problems. The original BOLT work received the Best Student Paper Award at IEEE ICASSP 2025.

- **BOLT: Universal Classifier Training via a Bayes-Error Upper Bound**, Mohammadreza Tavasoli Naeini, Ali Bereyhi, Morteza Noshad, Ben Liang, Alfred O. Hero III | 2026 | [Link](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.07754>)

- **Revisiting GAN with Bayes-Optimal Discrimination**, Mohammadreza Tavasoli Naeini, Ali Bereyhi, Morteza Noshad, Ben Liang, Alfred O. Hero III | 2026 | [Link](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.25609>)

## Communication-Efficient Distributed Learning

Communication overhead is a major bottleneck in distributed learning, particularly over wireless networks. Our research addresses this challenge through the development of communication-efficient techniques, including _gradient sparsification, device scheduling,_ and _over-the-air aggregation._ Beyond reducing communication costs, we investigate the fundamental role of aggregation errors in distributed learning. In particular, our _Global Unknown Estimation_ framework interprets distributed aggregation as a statistical estimation problem, highlighting that conventional computation-error metrics do not necessarily reflect the impact of aggregation on learning performance. Instead, the bias and variance of aggregation errors provide a more meaningful characterization, motivating new approaches to the design and optimization of distributed learning systems.

- **Global Unknown Estimation: A Statistical Framework for Wireless Distributed Learning**, Yicheng Qu, Ali Bereyhi, Ben Liang  
*IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC)* | 2026 | [Link](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02891>)

- **Regularized Top-k: A Bayesian Framework for Gradient Sparsification**, Ali Bereyhi, Ben Liang, Gary Boudreau, Ali Afana  
*IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing* | 2025 | [Link](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05633>)


## Intelligent Communications and Sensing Systems

Many problems in signal processing share mathematical structures with those encountered in machine learning, creating opportunities to leverage learning-inspired techniques for efficient system design and optimization. Our research explores these connections to address various challenges in wireless communications and sensing, including _array design, precoding, resource allocation,_ and _object detection_. UUtilizing machine learning techniques along with model-based signal processing, we develop computationally-efficient approaches to address key design problems in these domains.

- **Fast Tuning of Pinching Antenna-Assisted ISAC Systems via User Clustering**, Ruizhi Niu, Ali Bereyhi  
*IEEE Global Communications Conference (GLOBECOM)* | 2026 | [Link](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06492>)
- **Dynamic and static energy efficient design of pinching antenna systems**, Saba Asaad, Chongjun Ouyang, Ali Bereyhi, Zhiguo Ding  
*IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC)* | 2026 | [Link](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.08720>)
- **MIMO-PASS: Uplink and Downlink Transmission via MIMO Pinching-Antenna Systems**, Ali Bereyhi, Chongjun Ouyang, Saba Asaad, Zhiguo Ding, H. Vincent Poor  
*IEEE Transactions on Communications* | 2026 | [Link](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03117>)


## Learning-Based Optimization and Decision-Making

Recent advances in machine learning have opened new opportunities for addressing complex problems in prediction, optimization, and decision-making. Our research investigates how modern learning paradigms, including foundation models, generative modeling, and reinforcement learning, can be leveraged to address such challenges. We are particularly interested in understanding the capabilities and limitations of these approaches and developing methods that improve their effectiveness, reliability, and adaptability in real-world applications, with a particular emphasis on finance and automation.

- **Understanding Large Language Models as Numerical Optimizers**, Lingyun Guo, Ali Bereyhi | 2026 | [Link](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37932>) 
- **Regime-aware financial volatility forecasting via in-context learning**, Saba Asaad, Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Ali Bereyhi  
*FinAI Workshop at International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)* | 2026 | [Link](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.10299>)
